idea-plugin.name: TabCue: Visual Terminal Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Style terminal tabs with custom colours, background hints, and emojis so you can tell terminals and AI agents apart at a glance.

I kept losing track of which terminal was which — npm run dev, a couple of Claude sessions, and an ssh into something I would rather not typo in. They all look identical. So each Terminal tab can now have its own colour, icon or emoji.

Right-click any Terminal tab and choose Tab Style.

What it does

  • Colours — eight presets, or any colour at all from the IDE's own picker. Shown as the tab background and as a small dot.
  • Text colour — white, black or custom, for when you want a tab to stand out while you are looking at it.
  • Icons and emoji — a built-in icon or any emoji, from the tab menu.
  • Rules — style tabs automatically by title or working directory. Paint anything matching ssh prod red so you always know which machine you are on.
  • Background tint — optionally tint the terminal output area too, not just the tab.

It works before you configure anything. A new project starts with rules for Claude Code, Codex, Junie and aider, each with its own colour and emoji, and auto-assigned colours give every other terminal a colour derived from its own name and directory — so it is the same colour tomorrow.

Good to know

  • The IDE throws away a tab's colour while that tab is selected, so the dot, the emoji and the text colour are the cues that survive in every state.
  • Split terminals share one colour — a split is several sessions inside a single tab.
  • Rules live in .idea/terminalTabStyle.xml so you can commit and share them. Per-tab styles go in workspace.xml, because their keys contain local paths. Nothing leaves your machine.
